extracted.intended_audience: NLP / computational linguistics researchers and practitioners working on political bias detection and news-article classification
extracted.subtask_short: predicting political ideology of news articles
extracted.subtask_description: Designing datasets, models, and evaluation protocols to predict the political ideology (left/center/right) of news articles, with emphasis on generalization to unseen media sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manually annotated ideology dataset
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect and release a large dataset of articles that were manually annotated for political ideology — left, center, or right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper reports a dataset of 34,737 articles. Manual annotation and public release are emphasized to support research and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance across topics and media
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the dataset is well-balanced across both topics and media so that class distributions and topical/media confounds do not bias models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors state the dataset is well-balanced across topics and media, which is important to avoid models exploiting topical or source frequency instead of ideology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Out-of-source (unseen-media) evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a challenging experimental setup where test examples come from media that were not seen during training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents the model from learning to detect the source of the target news article instead of predicting its political ideology, and tests true generalization across outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adversarial media adaptation
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply adversarial adaptation methods to reduce media/source-specific signals and improve cross-media generalization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper proposes an adversarial media adaptation approach as a modeling strategy for handling media-domain shifts when predicting ideology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specially adapted triplet loss
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a specially adapted triplet loss to learn representations tailored to the ideology prediction task.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The triplet loss is adapted for this task (details in the paper) to encourage representations that separate ideological classes while handling intra-source variation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include background/source information as features
rubrics_metrics.description: Augment article-level inputs with background information about the source/publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors find that adding background information about the source is quite helpful for improving article-level prediction — incorporate source metadata when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare to strong pre-trained Transformer baselines
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate proposed methods against state-of-the-art pre-trained Transformers as baselines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper reports sizable improvements over using state-of-the-art pre-trained Transformers in the challenging unseen-media setup — use strong baselines to validate gains.
